raw_message.reasoning:
The /tmp/parse_modified.py has all the features. But my R3 test showed it didn't work - let me check what _validate_braces actually does and why it didn't raise an error for `{abc}`.

Actually, looking at the test I ran: `p = parse.Parser('{abc}')` - this is a valid format string where `{abc}` is a named field. The braces ARE properly enclosed in this case. The requirement says "a part containing braces is not fully enclosed within matching braces" - so something like `{abc` (missing closing brace) or `abc}` (missing opening brace) should fail.

Let me verify with a bad example.
